name: Mann–Whitney U rank statistic and test
definition: U_X=Σ_i Σ_j [1(X_i>Y_j)+0.5·1(X_i=Y_j)]; under the equal-distribution independent-sample null E[U_X]=nm/2.
variables: X_i and Y_j observations, n and m sample sizes, 1 indicator function; U_X pairwise rank statistic
assumptions: Independent groups and independent observations; use a null reference appropriate to ties and sample size.
limitations: Not generally a test of median equality; paired or serially dependent observations require a different design.
failure_conditions: Using an exact continuous no-ties null reference with tied data
computation: Rank the pooled sample with midranks and subtract n(n+1)/2 from the X rank sum; select a justified null reference separately.

name: Welch two-sample t-test
variables: n,m≥2 sample sizes; sample means mean_X,mean_Y; unbiased sample variances s_X²,s_Y²; ν approximate degrees of freedom
assumptions: Independent observations and independent samples, positive combined standard error, normality or adequate large-sample approximation; equal population variances not required.
limitations: Heavy tails and small skewed samples can impair approximation; not suited to paired forecast errors.
failure_conditions: Zero combined standard error or unmodelled dependence
computation: Compute sample moments, t statistic and Welch–Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; use approximate t reference for the mean-equality null.

name: Mean-centred Levene variance test
variables: k≥2 groups, n_i group sizes, N total size, z absolute deviations from group mean, W approximate F statistic
assumptions: Independent groups and observations, nonzero within-group deviation sum of squares, N>k; mean-centred version appropriate mainly for symmetric moderately tailed samples.
limitations: Approximate F reference can be poor under severe skew, heavy tails or small samples; no proof of equal variances from non-rejection.
computation: Compute absolute deviations from group means then apply one-way ANOVA statistic; use approximate F(k−1,N−k) reference.
